patches.value: For each 0<=r<=lambda<p, r! is invertible modulo p, so X_r and Y_r on the reduced module are the respective nonzero scalar multiples 1/r! of x^r and y^r; for r=0 the scalar is 1. The matrix-unit identities from S002 persist after reduction: their coefficients binom(lambda,j) are nonzero modulo p, and the same identities hold as operators on the K-basis b_0,...,b_lambda corresponding to the characteristic-zero e-basis. Thus any K-subspace W invariant under x and y is invariant under every E_i,j. Let W be arbitrary. If W=0, it is the zero subspace. For the other case, temporarily assume L1: W is nonzero. By the definition of nonzero subspace, there exists a vector w in W with w nonzero; record this existence before selecting w in S006.

value.statement: There exists w in W such that w is nonzero.

value.text: By existential elimination applied to the existence fact F002, choose a witness w in W with w nonzero; its private identity is used only in this branch. Since b_0,...,b_lambda were established in S004 as a K-basis of M tensor_Z K, there are unique scalars c_0,...,c_lambda in K with w=sum_i c_i b_i. At least one coefficient is nonzero, since if all c_i were zero the displayed expansion would give w=0, contrary to the witness property. Choose an index i in the range 0<=i<=lambda with c_i nonzero; establish this existential fact before selecting i.

produces.statement: There exists an index i with 0<=i<=lambda and c_i is nonzero.

value.text: By existential elimination from F003 choose such an index i. For every j with 0<=j<=lambda, matrix-unit action gives E_j,i w=c_i b_j. Because W is invariant under x and y it is invariant under E_j,i, so E_j,i w lies in W. The scalar c_i is nonzero in the field K and hence invertible; since W is a K-subspace, b_j=c_i^{-1}E_j,i w lies in W. This holds for each basis vector b_j, so W is the whole module. The chosen w and i are used only under L1.

The zero-subspace branch and the branch under L1 both establish that W is either zero or the whole module; discharge L1 by the two-case argument. The module has dimension lambda+1, which is positive because lambda>=0, so it is nonzero. Therefore it is irreducible as stated, including lambda=0 and p=2.

value.declaration: Temporarily assume that the arbitrary invariant subspace W is nonzero; this assumption is discharged by the zero/nonzero case argument.
Choose w in W with w nonzero using the earlier local existence fact F002.

value.type: K-scalar coordinates of w in the b-basis
value.declaration: Define the unique coordinates c_i in K by the expansion of the already selected vector w in the already established K-basis b_0,...,b_lambda.
Choose i with 0<=i<=lambda and c_i nonzero using the local existence fact F003.
